We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide (trans). So structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: an anilide where the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl (para) attached to phenyl with side chain: CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH (aniline). So three disconnections: 1) disconnection of sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (the phenyl with sulfonyl). 2) disconnection of amide formation: break C-N amide bond to give carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline. 3) disconnection of α,β-unsaturated acid formation via Doebner modification: break C=C double bond to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So retrosynthetic step: the α,β-unsaturated acid fragment (CH=CH-COOH) could be derived from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid. But our target has amide not acid; we will later convert acid to amide. So step 3: break the C=C and C=O to give aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with sulfonyl) and malonic acid. However the aromatic aldehyde is same phenyl as the one bearing sulfonyl? Actually the side chain is attached to that phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has the side chain at para? Not important.

Thus propose route:

Target (T)

Step 1 (retro): amide formation -> precursor A: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (same phenyl with side chain but COOH instead of CONH-Ph-NH). So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait need COOH attached to double bond: /C=C/C(=O)O (acid). So A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1

Step 2 (retro): Doebner modification -> break α,β-unsaturated acid to aromatic aldehyde (same phenyl with aldehyde) plus malonic acid. So precursor B: aromatic aldehyde: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde). plus malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) as simple building block.

Step 3 (retro): sulfonamide formation -> break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (the phenyl with aldehyde). So precursor C: sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1 (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline derivative: c1ccc(/C=O)cc1 (para? Actually the phenyl bearing aldehyde). So final precursors are commercially available: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, 4-formyl phenyl (or 4-formyl phenyl) maybe 4-formyl phenyl? Actually the phenyl attached to sulfonyl is the same as the one bearing aldehyde; it's a phenyl ring with aldehyde para to sulfonyl? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl at position 1 (sulfonyl attached to N). The side chain attaches at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 indicates substitution at position 1? Not needed.

Thus we can propose route with three reactions:

1) Amide coupling: carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) + 3-aminophenyl (aniline) using DCC/HATU to give amide.

2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid under basic conditions to give α,β-unsaturated acid.

3) Sulfonamide formation: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the aromatic aldehyde) to give sulfonamide.

Now we need to produce JSON with nested children: root molecule, then reaction nodes each with template_id. We need template IDs. We can search for templates for each reaction type.

Search for sulfonamide formation template: functional groups broken: primary amines, sulfonyl chloride? But sulfonyl chloride not in list. Could use "sulfonamides" formed. Let's search for templates where functional_groups_formed includes "sulfonamides".
